title: DeepSeek V4 Pro optional Cloud provider
objective: Enable the already-prepared DeepSeek provider only behind the existing authenticated, enabled and consented Cloud gate, using a backend-only configurable transport and an explicit session-only provider selection, while preserving the local default, exact-local fallback and the Desktop no-secret boundary.

included: Enable DeepSeek as a provider only when its backend configuration is complete and valid; otherwise it remains unavailable and Cloud falls back to Local.

Implement a backend-only DeepSeek HTTP seam and a deterministic fake-transport test seam. The request uses the existing bounded rewrite prompt and the response is routed through the existing Cloud output validation.
Read only DEEPSEEK_MODEL, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL from backend process configuration. No default model, key, endpoint, or secret is embedded in Desktop code or tests.

Constrain DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL, when configured, to the HTTPS origin https://api.deepseek.com with no userinfo, query, fragment, non-standard port or path. Derive the provider route locally rather than accepting a request-controlled endpoint.
Return 503 when the explicitly requested provider is unavailable after request validation, preserving the established backend unavailable-provider response semantics.

Add a session-only explicit Gemini/DeepSeek provider selection to the existing Cloud settings and Profiles presentation. The selection starts at Gemini, is not persisted, is never logged, and cannot enable Cloud or grant consent.
Keep all existing authentication, consent, Cloud enablement, backend availability, output validation, observability redaction, exact-local fallback and target-safe insertion behavior unchanged.

Add unit, integration and source-security tests covering provider selection, unavailable configuration, request construction without secret exposure, failure fallback, cancellation, DeepSeek non-selection by default, and Gemini regression.
Document the trust boundary, operational prerequisite and a manual server-only configuration checklist without copying any credential.
excluded: Reading, modifying, printing, committing or automatically loading .env, .env.*, secrets, credentials, API keys, tokens, certificates or account data.
Supabase, Google, DeepSeek, GitHub or hosting-account configuration; account login; API call; live smoke; billing; deployment; publication; or Git mutation.
Any provider key, endpoint, model identifier, or OAuth material in the WPF Desktop, repository configuration, test fixture, logs or UI.

Automatic Gemini-to-DeepSeek or DeepSeek-to-Gemini fallback, background retry, automatic Cloud enablement, automatic consent, provider selection persistence, telemetry expansion or user-content logging.
Changes to local transcription, local rewriting behavior, dictionary persistence, insertion, hotkey, capsule, password protection, Supabase PKCE, refresh-token storage or existing Fluent local data.
New NuGet packages, registry changes, administrator installation or command-line secret tooling.

acceptanceCriteria: DeepSeek is unavailable unless valid backend-only process configuration is present; a missing, malformed or rejected configuration cannot send a network request and reports a controlled unavailable result.
The Desktop defaults to Gemini and requires an explicit session-only user selection before it can request DeepSeek. Authentication, Cloud enablement and consent remain independently required.
The backend provider never returns a secret, logs a secret or emits user text. HTTP authorization is a request header, never a query string. HTTP client logging is disabled for the provider client.
A provider error, invalid response, cancellation, disabled state or output-validation failure retains the exact local result; no cross-provider automatic fallback exists.
DeepSeek receives the same bounded prompt and equivalent output-validation protection as Gemini, with source tests for protected tokens and no secret/config loader in Desktop code.
Focused tests, full restore/build/test, required architecture/security/privacy/test reviews and final Development Judge evidence pass. The result remains IMPLEMENTED_AWAITING_USER_REVIEW.
No live DeepSeek call, account configuration, secret entry, deployment, Git change or external mutation is performed in this task.
requiredTests: Desktop provider selection defaults, rejects unavailable selection, remains session-only and never enables Cloud or grants consent
DeepSeek Desktop transport routing only after explicit selection and full Cloud gate; Gemini/default and Local fallback regression
Backend DeepSeek configuration, exact origin validation, unavailable behavior, request shape/header redaction, HTTP failure, cancellation and empty/invalid response
Cloud output validation and exact-local fallback parity for DeepSeek
Source scans for .env loading, provider secret/model/endpoint leakage to Desktop, authorization query parameters, provider logging and automatic cross-provider fallback
risks: A provider credential, endpoint or model could leak into the Desktop, repository, test output or logs.
A malformed backend base URL could become server-side request forgery.
A provider selection could bypass authentication, consent or the local-first fallback.
A DeepSeek response could be unsafe or a failure could replace the local result.
A real configuration, live call, billing event or deployment could be inferred without user authority.
rollbackPlan: Set DeepSeek capabilities and server availability back to disabled, leaving Gemini and Local behavior untouched.
Remove only the session-only selection UI and its local code; do not alter authentication, persisted dictionary or existing user data.
Keep the backend configuration absent to retain default-deny behavior without touching secrets.
dependencies: User message on 2026-07-21 validating continuation, interpreted as approval for this bounded offline DeepSeek preparation and prior Phase 06B review; no external operation is implied.
ADR-0005 optional Cloud rewrite and Phase 07B authentication boundaries.
A later separate user-authorized server configuration, backend deployment and controlled live smoke are required to exercise DeepSeek.
humanApprovals: The user explicitly validated continuation on 2026-07-21 after being informed that DeepSeek is the next optional Cloud phase and that server-only key/cost authorization is required.
No authorization exists for reading .env, entering a key, account setup, billing, live provider invocation, deployment or Git publication.
